chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who misses (someone in his absence) is himself missed (by others), and the one who does not prepare patience against the calamities of time will be frustrated, and the one who troubles the people will be troubled by them, and the one who leaves them alone will not be left alone by them.' It was said, 'So what shall I do, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Lend them from your dignity for the day of your poverty.'
ai.seo_question: How can one prepare for future poverty and maintain dignity according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of al-Kulayni’s al-Kafi, underscores the reciprocal nature of social conduct, linking patience (sabr) with the preservation of one's honor (ird). It advises that by lending one's dignity through generosity and respect to others, one secures a reserve of honor for future times of need, reflecting the Shia emphasis on mutual rights and social harmony.

en.hubeali: H 14495 – Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzaal, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Al-Jaroud: Abu Ja’farasws said:

‘The Messenger<sup>saww</sup> of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> said: ‘The one who misses (someone in his absence) is himself missed (by others), and the one who does not prepare (himself to observe) patience against the ravages of the time would be frustrated, and the one who problems the people would be troubled by them, and the one who leaves them (under troubles) alone would not be left alone by them (but troubles will be returned to him)’. It was said, ‘So what shall I do, O Messenger<sup>saww</sup> of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>?’ He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Lend them from you dignity, from the little you have and from what you need (for yourself) to (them)’.
